newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aims to bring Kurds to negotiating table.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aims to bring Kurds to negotiating table.

text.p: A senior U.S. official is expected to meet Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani on Thursday and it is hoped talks with rival Kurdish leader Jalal Talabani can also be arranged in the future, the State Department said on Tuesday.

"Our objective is to have Mr. Barzani and Mr. Talabani agree to talk about their differences peacefully and across from one another at the negotiating table," State Department spokesman Nicholas BUrns told reporters.

"The meeting on Thursday (between Barzani and Assistant Secretary Robert Pelletreau) will not be a trilateral meeting ... We do hope it will be possible for the United States to arrange a meeting with Mr. Talabani in the future," he said.

U.S. officials for several years had been working to bring the two main Kurdish factions in northern Iraq into a stable political reconciliation. But those talks broke down on Aug. 30 and the two sides resumed fighting, with Barzani winning control of the region with the assistance of Iraqi forces.
The United States subsequently launched air strikes against targets in southern Iraq in an effort to curb further military moves by President Saddam Hussein.
Burns said Washington moved to resume its diplomatic activity after receiving a letter from Barzani more than one week ago.
He said it was uncertain where the Barzani-Pelletreau meeting would take place, but an Iraqi opposition group reported that the venue would be Turkey.
Burns said Pelletreau had a "detailed agenda" to discuss with Barzani, but refused to lay it all out publicly.

"The United States will repeat our very deeply held concerns about the situation in Northern Iraq, about the lack of stability caused by the fighting, about our concern for Kurds and other ethnic groups in Northern Iraq and about the humanitarian situation in Northern Iraq," Burns said.

Also Pelletreau "will certainly repeat the advice privately that we have tried to give Mr. Barzani and Mr. Talabani in public and that is that Mr. Barzani's relationship with Saddam Hussein cannot be in the long term interest of his people or himself," Burns added.
